descriptions.text: Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie. The second smallest of the chains of leadership, it is still considered a great honor to be the custodian of this burden. Each jewel encrusted upon this charm represents a settlement owned and controlled by the bearer. If one still maintains a settlement's jewel upon the collapse of the level, the holder of this necklace will permanently receive a tax stipend every ten days from that settlement based on size and population. […] One Attached Gem: Poor Sapphire. Medium Skyfowl Settlement (Third Floor). +5 to Dexterity. +Talon Strike (Level 5) Taxes received: 432 Gold every 10 days. May you be a kind and just leader.

beats.headline: From the Tyrant's box
beats.text: Becoming the town's new magistrate earned Carl a Platinum Tyrant's Box, and it holds 10,000 gold and a necklace: a simple silver-coloured chain, a quarter-sized charm, a tiny yellow jewel. It is the second smallest of the chains of leadership. Each jewel is a settlement the bearer controls, and one still held when the level collapses pays a tax stipend every ten days for good. To upgrade it he would have to conquer a large settlement. Carl guesses that explains why the townsfolk never recognised him as their leader: he probably had to put it on first. When he does, he gains five dexterity and the Talon Strike skill, and tucks it under his shirt. It feels heavier than it should.

beats.headline: A sliver of amethyst
beats.text: Killing a mayor has earned Carl a gold Tyrant's box. It holds a sliver of an amethyst, smaller than the poor sapphire already on his necklace, and it gives him three points of dexterity and nothing else. Donut's red gem on her own leadership charm gave two intelligence, one dexterity and a few points in a spear-throwing skill she will never use, and its small settlement pays her only 403 gold every ten days, which annoys her.
